News.title: Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ in broad daylight attack at country park – as cops hunt man in his 30s
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PARK HORROR Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ in broad daylight attack at country park – as cops hunt man in his 30s

A WOMAN was allegedly sexually assaulted at a park in a sickening broad daylight attack.

Cops said they have stepped up patrols in the area as detectives hunt a man described as white and aged in his 30s.

The sexual assault reportedly happened in a wooded area of Newstead and Annesley Country Park in Nottinghamshire.

The force said the incident occurred shortly after 11am on Tuesday (August 4).





Officers have launched a major investigation and increased their presence in the area.

Detective Inspector Ed Cook, of Nottinghamshire Police, has sought to reassure the community.

He said: “While incidents of this nature are extremely rare, they are obviously very concerning for the public.

“I would like to reassure people we have a large team of officers working on this investigation and we are doing everything we can to find the person responsible.

“The suspect has been described as a white man aged in his 30s.

“Public safety remains our top priority and extra patrols will continue to be carried out in the area.

“I’d also encourage the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious or concerning behaviour to us immediately.”

Police have urged anyone who saw anything suspicious around the time of the attack to come forward.



Officers are also appealing for anyone with information which could help identify the suspect to contact them.

Anyone with information is asked to call Nottinghamshire Police on 101, quoting incident number 38 of 7 August.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Terrifying moment huge hippo charges at boat full of tourists as beast lunges out of the water in pursuit
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a huge hippo charges at a boat packed with tourists before lunging through the water in a furious pursuit.

Viral footage captures the heart-stopping moment the massive male beast suddenly gives chase in Botswana, forcing the fleeing boat to speed away.



The tourists had been hoping for a glimpse of Africa’s spectacular wildlife when they spotted the lone hippo in the distance.

But their thrilling wildlife encounter quickly turned into a terrifying battle to escape the enormous beast.



The captain slowed the boat to avoid disturbing the territorial animal before issuing a chilling warning to his passengers.

Oznur Bell, the tourist who captured the moment on camera said: “After watching his behaviour for a moment, he calmly said, ‘Hold on-we need to speed up now before he decides to come after us.’

“The moment we accelerated, we looked back and realized the hippo was chasing us.”

The shocking footage shows the hulking animal powering through the water as it relentlessly pursues the boat.

For several terrifying moments, the tourists were left staring back at the furious beast as it bobbed in and out of the water behind them.

The videographer said: “For a few moments, every single person in the boat was genuinely worried.”



Oznur described the terrifying encounter as “one of the most terrifying moments I’ve ever experienced.”

According to the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, common hippos can grow to a staggering 16.5ft long and 5.2ft tall at the shoulder.

Adult males can weigh between 3,500 and almost 10,000lbs – making the colossal mammals roughly the weight of a mid-length SUV.

Despite their fearsome size and reputation, hippos are herbivores and do not view humans as prey.

Researchers at the University of Pretoria say hippos kill around 500 people across Africa every year – more than twice as many as lions.



The enormous animals are territorial and can aggressively defend their patches of water.

That means an unsuspecting boat entering their territory can quickly become a dangerous target.

The monstrous male eventually called off the chase, allowing the shaken tourists to escape.

But the dramatic encounter also showcased the astonishing way hippos move through shallow water.

Rather than relying solely on traditional swimming strokes, the powerful animals can propel themselves by pushing off the bottom in a bizarre galloping or bounding motion.



The furious hippo put the remarkable technique on full display as it thundered through the water after the fleeing boat.

News.title: Are twisted Russian civilians PAYING drone pilots to carry out sick ‘human safari’ attacks on innocent Ukrainians?
News.content:
TWISTED Russian civilians have been accused of paying for sick “human safari” hunting missions targeting defenceless Ukrainians on the streets.

Drone pilots working within the Russian army are “wilfully targeting civilians for monetary gain” under Vladimir Putin‘s evil rule, a former Nato analyst told The Sun.



Terrifying footage this week showed Yuriy, a 52-year-old grocer, running for his life as he was chased down by a Kremlin suicide drone.

The Ukrainian was left with serious shrapnel wounds as the UAV exploded as it struck the grocer’s tent where he was selling fruit and vegetables.



Harrowing footage was released just a few days later and captured another drone attack on a Ukrainian civilian in Sumy.

A Russian drone pursues a local appearing to toy with him before the operator makes the drone explode in a huge blast.

The horror scenes make up just a couple of the thousands of senseless attacks on civilians by Russia during the war in Ukraine with Kherson becoming known as the grim epicentre of the attacks.

Dr Patrick Bury, a warfare and counter-terrorism expert and former Nato analyst, says the brutality highlights how Putin has created a regime which is “completely rotten to the core”.



He told The Sun: “[Russia is] going in and they’re basically intentionally targeting civilians.

“It’s become known as the Kherson safari, essentially civilian hunting missions.

“It shows we’re at the real bottom of the barrel of human conduct in war.”

Dr Bury says the human safaris would be considered one of the worst atrocities committed by Moscow should they ever face consequences.

The term human safari is most well known due to the 1990s siege of Sarajevo.



Wealthy tourists were accused of making weekend trips to the besieged city and paying Serbian fighters to shoot civilians in the streets.

Dr Bury fears a similar pattern of abuse could be repeated in Ukraine after several worrying reports from independent journalists in Kyiv.

He claims: “It looks like a fusion between military units like the eighth Artillery Regiment and certain people in there who are drone operators.



“They have been accused of using crowdfunding from Russian civilians to gain money.

“They’re wilfully targeting civilians for monetary gain and propaganda gain.

“The fact that there’s been no one brought to task speaks volumes about the Russian military – the laws of war are clearly not a priority for them.”

In Kherson alone, Human Rights Watch (HRW) found at least 45 drone strikes carried out by Russian forces that appeared to deliberately target civilians.

Dozens of these cases were filmed and shared across Russian social media and Telegram channels.



In almost every example seen, HRW claims they believe the drone operator was purposely targeting a civilian or civilian infrastructure like a bus or parking lot.

Intentionally killing civilians during an armed conflict is a serious war crime, under international humanitarian law, such as the Geneva Conventions.

A United Nations probe during the conflict has found Russia guilty of committing crimes against humanity in the occupied regions of Ukraine.



The UN report states that large numbers of Ukrainian civilians have been targeted in a “widespread and systematic manner” at the hands of Russia.

Ukraine’s former deputy minister at the Ministry of Internal Affairs Anton Gerashchenko also condemned the human hunts.

He blasted: “Russian human safari is spreading. Russia‘s war crimes are mounting up.”

Back in April, three separate strikes on public spaces in the Nikopol district killed 10 and injured over 50 civilians within three days.

Russian FPVs hit two passenger buses, killing four civilians while a second in the nearby Chervonohryhorivka municipality wounded five.



A drone also struck a civilian car, killing one and injuring another as a day earlier five were killed when a Kremlin drone struck a civilian market in Nikopol.

Much like this year, the number of civilian attacks often surges in summer, Dr Bury says.

“Between summer 2025 and by October 2025, it was up to about 200 confirmed dead and over 2,000 wounded in these kinds of attacks.

“And they’re targeting everyone, they’re targeting shops, people going out for a cigarette, children in playgrounds even people on their way home from work.”

One of the scariest parts of these attacks is how defenceless the civilians are when the deadly UAVs lock onto their positions.



The drones can be operated by a soldier who watches a camera which allows them to track a target even if they try to run or hide.

“It’s not as if civilians in these areas are equipped with electromagnetic jammers so you can hear them and take cover and that is about it,” Dr Bury added.

For experts such as Patrick, the fact Russians allegedly partake in such heinous activities comes down to the example set by their despotic leader.

Dr Bury said: “There’s a lot of great things that have come out of Russia but ultimately it is quite a brutalised place, especially since the Soviets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And certainly in this war, you get to the front line and you’re put into a meat storm where you’re given a gun and then just told to charge the enemy to be quickly wiped down in a human wave attack.



“I think all this plays into a kind of normalisation of this kind of brutal behaviour.”

News.title: Scots child rapist found after escaping from day out at health clinic
News.content:
BEAST FOUND Scots child rapist found after escaping from day out at health clinic

A CONVICTED child rapist has been found after escaping from a health clinic during a day out.

Sicko Clifford Lyons Dobbie, 54, absconded from the Rohallion Secure Care Clinic in Perth on Thursday afternoon.



It is believed the depraved paedo slipped staff supervision while on a trip to the city centre.

A major police manhunt was launched to locate the beast – whose victims include a 10-year-old schoolgirl, a boy of 12 and a male hospital patient with learning difficulties.



Cops released CCTV pics of the fiend and warned the public not to approach him.

It is understood he was accompanied by his girlfriend, when he vanished from staff supervision on a trip to the city centre.

However cops confirmed this morning the beast had been located.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We are pleased to confirm Cliff Lyons Dobbie has been traced.”



A source previously told the Scottish Sun of the huge “security blunder” left locals beyond belief.

They said: “The thought of a dangerous paedophile roaming around near young children and vulnerable people is deeply unsettling.

“ How on earth was he allowed out in the first place?

“This is a huge security blunder.”

We told previously of the outrage after Lyons was spotted mingling with unsuspecting shoppers during an escorted day trip to Ayr in 2020 while held at the town’s Priory Clinic.



The monster was first caged at Carstairs State Hospital in 1990 after admitting to the rape of a 10-year-old girl in a field near his home in Drumchapel, Glasgow.

The twisted pervert was on bail at the time after luring a 12-year-old boy into a field and forcing him to strip.

Lyons previously tried to abscond after being transferred to Lennox Castle Hospital in Glasgow, before being returned to Carstairs.

In 2007, security restrictions were put on him after he was caught abusing a vulnerable male patient inside the high-security facility.

The dangerous predator has now spent more than 35 years locked away in institutions.



We previously revealed how the monster struck up a relationship with NHS Tayside bank worker Marina Kinnie after meeting her inside a secure clinic.

Eyewitnesses claimed the fiend was seen throwing popcorn down Ms Kinnie’s top as the pair tucked into takeaways together.

It is claimed she even sent the predator a photo of herself and her family – including two young children.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The beast saved the snap on his phone before an orderly spotted the images and raised the alarm at Rohallion.

Twice-divorced Ms Kinnie was then sacked from her job.

News.title: ‘Loving’ dad, 44, killed after being hit by six vehicles including cop car on major A-road is pictured as tributes paid
News.content:
