Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: How far is modern F1 like the ‘turbo era’? | Formula 1
Conor Benn Has Built-In Escape Hatch For Ryan Garcia Fight, Says Simon Jordan
Sports.content:
“Has he got a built-in excuse?” Jordan said on talkSPORT Boxing.

Jordan described what Benn can say if the weight cut takes too much out of him and Garcia wins.

“If he goes down to 147 and Ryan Garcia deals with him, he can turn around and say, ‘I was washed out of this fight at this weight. I thought I could do it, I can’t.’”

There is an obvious reason Benn is willing to take that chance. Ryan offers him a far bigger financial opportunity than the alternatives waiting at 154 pounds. Jaron “Boots” Ennis, Sebastian Fundora and Josh Kelly offer difficult fights without bringing the commercial appeal Ryan does. A fight with Ryan gives Benn the chance at another major payday after his two lucrative bouts with Eubank.

Benn may also see a physical advantage worth pursuing. He is naturally the bigger fighter. Provided the weight cut does not leave him depleted, he can put substantial weight back on after making 147, leaving Garcia to deal with a heavier opponent on fight night.

The upside makes the risk worthwhile. Make 147 cleanly, rehydrate, and Benn gets Garcia with a potential size advantage alongside a major purse.

If the weight cut drains him and Garcia wins, Benn can move straight to 154 pounds afterward. That is where Jordan’s point lands: the explanation for a loss at 147 is already available.

Sports.title: Muhammad Ali vs. Joe Frazier III: The 15th Round That Never Happened
Sports.content:
Ali took command during the closing stretch. Frazier’s face was severely swollen, his vision heavily compromised, and Ali repeatedly landed clean right hands. Futch had seen enough, stopping the fight before the 15th round began.

Frazier protested. He had spent his career walking through punishment to get close enough to land his left hook, and quitting voluntarily was never an option.

Futch’s responsibility was different. He had to decide if sending a fighter who could barely see back into the ring was worth the risk.

Ali Was Near His Limit Too

What Futch could not fully know was the physical state of the man in the opposite corner.

Ali survived a ferocious stretch in the middle rounds as Frazier attacked his body and forced exhausting exchanges. The oppressive heat inside the arena made the physical toll even worse.

Ali later described Manila as the closest he had ever come to dying.

“It was like death. Closest thing to dying that I know of,” Ali said to ESPN.

That admission has kept the hypothetical final round alive for decades. Frazier was in worse visible condition, but Ali was badly exhausted after spending enormous energy taking control of the fight again.

Frazier also understood how much punishment Ali had absorbed during their 14 rounds.

“Man, I hit him with punches that’d bring down the walls of a city. Lawdy, lawdy, he’s a great champion.”

Could Frazier have produced one final left hook? Would Ali have found the strength to continue punishing an opponent who could barely see? Or would those extra minutes simply have inflicted unnecessary damage on two fighters who had already given everything?

Futch Had Only One Fighter to Protect

The temptation is to look backward and wonder if Futch deprived Frazier of a final opportunity. From his position in the corner, however, the choice was simple.

Frazier was absorbing punches he was having increasing difficulty seeing. Futch couldn’t gamble his fighter’s health on the possibility that Ali was just as exhausted across the ring.

The stoppage gave Ali the victory and a 2-1 advantage in their trilogy. Frazier never fought Ali again.

Had Futch allowed the final round and Frazier somehow stopped Ali, their rivalry would be remembered differently. Frazier would have owned two victories over the most famous heavyweight of his generation, winning both the first and final fights of their trilogy.

Instead, the 15th round exists only in imagination.

Perhaps nothing would have changed. Ali may simply have continued what he had done in the 13th and 14th rounds.

After everything they had survived that morning in Manila, those remaining three minutes were an eternity.

Sports.title: Emmanuel Carrillo Jr. Stops Kenneth Taylor in Two Rounds
Sports.content:
Carrillo controlled the opening round before ending the fight in the second. A left hook to the chin dropped Taylor, who received a count from referee Rafael Ramos before the contest was stopped at the 1:00 mark.

The victory moved Carrillo to 7-0 with four knockouts. Taylor fell to 15-7-2 with six knockouts.

In the six-round featherweight co-feature, Ayanna “Asesina” Vasquez (8-2-1, 1 KO) defeated Maria “Polvorita” Salinas (27-16-6, 7 KOs). Vasquez countered effectively as Salinas pressed forward during the early rounds. Salinas became more competitive as the fight progressed, and both fighters traded freely in the sixth.

Christina Cruz (7-1) defeated Randee “Babydoll” Lynn Morales (6-8, 4 KOs) in a six-round super flyweight bout. Cruz controlled much of the action, consistently beating Morales to the punch and finishing the fight strongly.

Ariana Carrasco (2-0, 1 KO) remained perfect as a professional with a four-round decision over Chanisse Jenner (0-1). Carrasco controlled the fight from the opening round and won by identical scores of 40-36.

Devon Marquis Garcia (5-0, 4 KOs) defeated Patrick Harris (1-7, 1 KO) over four rounds. Harris became more competitive in the third, but Garcia finished strongly and dropped him with a right uppercut late in the fourth. The judges scored the bout 39-36 and 40-35 twice.

Cahir “The Gail” Gormley (4-0, 2 KOs) completed the card with a four-round decision over Jerome Lloyd (0-2-1). Gormley controlled the action with his boxing and won 40-36 on all three scorecards.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Petitions IBF For Lightweight Ranking Restoration
Sports.content:
Cruz held the No. 3 spot at lightweight before defeating Abraham Montoya on July 18. That placement kept him near the front of the line despite a majority decision loss to Muratalla in their January title fight.

The situation grew confusing following the Montoya victory. Cruz indicated publicly that he planned to compete at super featherweight, with Boxeo Mundial subsequently publishing comments attributed to him warning fighters in that weight class:

“Everyone at 130 pounds needs to be very careful with me, they already know. I’m ready for more challenges, it’s time to put on a show.”

Jake Donovan questioned Seda’s account, noting that someone was clearly communicating a move to 130 on the fighter’s behalf.

Returning to 135 provides Cruz a route to another title opportunity much sooner than starting over in a new weight class. Muratalla had already been struggling with the lightweight limit before his recent victory over Robson Conceição and is preparing to move to light welterweight.

Cruz’s former position is no longer available. In the IBF ratings released August 4, Artur Subkhankulov is No. 2, and Dzmitry Asanau has taken the No. 3 spot, while No. 1 remains vacant. Alan Abel Chaves is No. 4.

That leaves the IBF with a decision on where Cruz belongs if it grants his request. A position near the top would keep him within reach of the title if Muratalla vacates. Dropping Cruz farther down the rankings could mean a much longer route back, especially for a technically difficult opponent rival promoters may have little incentive to put in with their leading contenders.

Sports.title: Devin Haney, Jack Catterall In Advanced Talks For October 3
Sports.content:
Catterall brings a secondary title into the picture. The British southpaw won the WBA Regular welterweight belt by defeating Shakhram Giyasov by unanimous decision on May 23 at the Pyramids of Giza in Egypt. He dropped Giyasov in the opening round before winning by scores of 119-108, 118-109 and 116-111.

That victory put Catterall in position for a fight with Romero, the WBA’s primary welterweight champion. The sanctioning body ordered Romero to face Catterall within 180 days following the Giyasov victory.

An October 3 challenge against Haney would send Catterall down a different path before that window expires.

It creates an unusual situation at 147 pounds. Haney holds the WBO championship, while Rolly owns the primary WBA belt. Catterall possesses the secondary version. Haney-Catterall therefore would not be a true unification despite both fighters bringing titles into the ring.

Catterall has pursued Haney for years, dating back to their time at light welterweight. He now has an opportunity to finally land the matchup after moving to 147 and claiming his first world title.

The choice carries risk. Catterall already has a route to Romero, but facing Haney offers an immediate chance to capture the WBO belt while testing himself against one of the division’s biggest names.

Haney gets an established southpaw coming off a significant welterweight victory rather than waiting for another option to materialize. If negotiations are completed, Catterall’s long pursuit of Haney may take priority over the WBA title fight already waiting for him.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza-Lorenzo Parra Planned for Canelo-Mbilli Card
Sports.content:
Parra (24-1-1, 18 KOs) has worked his way to the No. 1 position in the WBO rankings at 126 pounds. That puts him directly in Espinoza’s path, providing the champion a mandatory defense after a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Espinoza (28-0, 24 KOs) has not fought since stopping Arnold Khegai in the 11th round last November. The 6’1″ Mexican champion Espinoza’s height, reach and power make him a problem for featherweights. There has not exactly been a rush among the division’s top fighters to pursue him.

Two-time Olympic gold medalist Robeisy Ramirez found out how punishing Espinoza can be when they met for a second time in December 2024. Espinoza stopped Ramirez in the sixth round after damaging his right eye, which was later diagnosed as a fractured orbital bone. Nearly two years later, Ramirez still has not fought again.

Parra’s No. 1 ranking makes him next in line for Espinoza’s belt. The 32-year-old Venezuelan earned his biggest recent victory in February, stopping Elijah Pierce in the second round to capture the WBO International featherweight title.

If finalized for the October event, Espinoza will return after nearly 12 months away from the ring. Parra would be fighting for a world title for the first time in his career.

Sports.title: Rolly Romero Claims Ryan Garcia Ducked Him Twice
Sports.content:
Rolly Romero has little interest in Ryan Garcia claiming he wants the winner of Romero’s fight with Teofimo Lopez, arguing that Garcia already passed on two chances to face him. Romero questioned why Garcia’s name even came up during discussions about his upcoming matchup.

“Didn’t he duck me twice? He ducked me after our direct rematch clause, and he ducked me after he fought Barrios,” Romero said to Fight Hub TV. “You’re going to tell me that this dude wants to fight or he’s just trying to chase whatever clout he can get right now? Same way he calls out everybody in the world and doesn’t fight anybody. Don’t bring up Ryan Garcia. He’s a clout-chasing fool.”

Romero defeated Garcia by unanimous decision in May 2025, dropping him in the second round and controlling enough of the action to win by scores of 115-112 twice and 118-109. A rematch never materialized, and Romero argues that Ryan had another chance after his fight with Mario Barrios but chose a different direction.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Avoided Opetaia Before Mikaelian Stepped Up
Sports.content:
“I would think if you’re David Benavidez, you’re supposed to carry yourself as the A-side. You think you’re the man. You’ve already headlined in Vegas, and that’s going to be your next date,” Mora told DAZN Boxing. “I’m thinking I’m the man, and then I get pushed aside by a Noel Mikaelian? Really? That’s what I would be upset at if I was David Benavidez. And then Jai Opetaia is the fight that we all want to see. Instead, you’re going to be hopefully turning to a Cieslak, a Polish fighter I’ve never heard of or seen fight before?”

That narrative makes it sound as though Mikaelian took an Opetaia fight Benavidez wanted. There has been little indication Benavidez was seriously pursuing it.

Opetaia has publicly called out Benavidez, accusing him this week of avoiding the matchup. When his fight with Mikaelian was announced, the Australian specifically singled out Benavidez.

“Credit to Noel for stepping up to the plate while others, yes, David Benavidez, I’m talking about you, continue to run and hide,” Opetaia said.

Benavidez had the opportunity to target Opetaia after moving to cruiserweight but chose to pursue other options. If he faces Cieslak next, Mikaelian cannot be blamed for pushing him out of an Opetaia fight he had not been pursuing.

Mora may be unaware of that history or simply chose not to mention it. Whatever the reason, his criticism misses the larger issue. Benavidez did not need Mikaelian to move aside. He could have pursued Opetaia himself.

Ghana News.title: UNIWIZ Foundation trains Greater Accra ICT coordinators in advanced digital skills
Ghana News.content:
ICT coordinators from districts across the Greater Accra Region have undergone a two-day Advanced Digital Skills Training programme aimed at strengthening digital literacy and enhancing the delivery of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) education in schools.

The training, which opened on Thursday, August 6, and ended on Friday August 7, at Methodist University, Dansoman, brought together ICT coordinators from across the region and selected ICT teachers from senior high schools to build their technical capacity through practical digital tools and strategies for teaching and learning.

Organised by the UNIWIZ Foundation in partnership with the Ghana Education Service (GES), ModePlus Innovation Hub and Intellite IT Solutions, with support from the Embassy of Switzerland in Ghana, the training was held on the theme, "Advancing Ghana's Education Technology Workforce."

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the UNIWIZ Foundation, Wisdom Larry Quarme-Doe, said although digital infrastructure is essential, it is educators who ultimately drive digital transformation in schools.

"Digital infrastructure and computers alone do not transform our children. People do. The true drivers of digital literacy in our schools are our ICT coordinators. You are the digital champions guiding the next generation into the global economy."

He said the two-day programme was designed to equip participants with practical knowledge and advanced digital tools that would improve the integration of technology into teaching and learning.

"This two-day intensive training is designed to equip you with advanced tools, practical skills and practical strategies to elevate educational technology across Ghana."

Mr Quarme-Doe urged participants to maximise the opportunity by learning from one another and embracing emerging technologies.

"Over the next two days, immerse yourselves, exchange ideas, challenge your limits and embrace new technologies. The knowledge you take back to your respective institutions will cascade directly to thousands of young Ghanaians."

Representing the Greater Accra Regional Director of Education, Regional Planning Officer Ahmed Alhassan described the programme as timely, noting that ICT continues to play an increasingly significant role in Ghana's education system.

"ICT has now become a core subject at the basic level and it is now an elective at the WASSCE level. That is why I think this training is so important because those who are providing education for these kids need to have advanced skills in ICT so that they can also impact the children."

He said continuous capacity-building for ICT coordinators and teachers is necessary to ensure they remain equipped to teach evolving digital skills.

"We need to always organise workshops for them to upgrade their knowledge and skills in ICT so that, at the end of it, it is the Ghanaian child who is in school that will be the biggest beneficiary of the programme."

Mr Alhassan observed that ICT education has improved over the years with the establishment of computer laboratories in many schools, although more infrastructure is still needed.

"Previously, when ICT was introduced as an examinable subject at the basic level, because of lack of equipment and ICT materials, teaching it was very difficult. You cannot teach ICT in an abstract."

He therefore called on organisations and development partners to support efforts to expand ICT facilities across schools.

"The issue is still about establishing more ICT labs in the schools. Government cannot do it all. Stakeholders who are willing to support the Ghanaian education system can come to our offices, and we can direct them to where we need these ICT labs, especially where we have clusters of schools."

According to the Embassy of Switzerland in Ghana they supported the training because it addresses the need to equip children with the digital skills required to thrive in today's world.

"The embassy is pleased to support this programme because it addresses some of the most important questions in our education sector today, information technology and how we ensure that children are equipped and ready for the world that they are in today."

They reminded participants that the knowledge gained should ultimately benefit learners.

"All of us gathered here are not the final recipients of this programme. I want to urge you to at all times keep in mind the children who are indeed the ultimate beneficiaries of such a training."

Highlighting the pace of technological advancement globally, the representative from the Embassy said Ghanaian children must be supported to remain competitive.

"We see them as athletes on the field, whereas ours are just about preparing in the dressing room to get on that track. That is how unfortunate the current situation is."

The two-day training combined presentations with practical sessions designed to strengthen participants' digital competencies and enhance the teaching of ICT across schools in the Greater Accra Region.

Ghana News.title: CUTS challenges DVLA over escalating ‘delinquency’ charges
Ghana News.content:
The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) is facing calls to suspend its escalating “delinquency” charges on expired driver’s licences until it publicly establishes the legal authority, approval process and formula used to determine the fees.

The demand has come from CUTS International, a public policy think tank, which argues that the charges lack clear backing in the Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180) and could unfairly penalise motorists whose licences have expired even when they have not driven during the period.

In a statement issued on August 9, 2026, the Director of the West Africa Regional Centre of CUTS International, Accra, Appiah Kusi Adomako, said the DVLA should disclose the precise statutory instrument and approved fee schedule authorising each charge.

Under the DVLA’s Summary of Licensing and Other Activity Rates for 2026, renewing a licence before its expiry costs GH¢127. However, the amount increases to GH¢204.25 for a licence expired by between one day and six months, GH¢279.25 for seven to 12 months, GH¢315.25 for up to two years, GH¢352.25 for up to four years and GH¢404.25 for more than four years.

CUTS said similar escalating charges applied to the replacement of expired licences.

“The DVLA must show Ghanaians the law, the approved fee schedule and the formula behind every cedi it collects as a delinquency charge. Public power must rest on law. If the Authority cannot point to a clear legal basis for each charge, it must stop collecting the money and refund affected licence holders,” Mr Adomako said.

Legal basis questioned

At the centre of CUTS’ objection is Regulation 33 of L.I. 2180, which provides for the renewal of a driver’s licence both before and after its expiry.

The organisation said the regulations expressly recognise that licences may be renewed after expiry and separately provide for an offence where a person fails to renew as prescribed.

Under the law, a person who fails to renew a driver’s licence as prescribed is liable, upon summary conviction, to a fine of between 10 and 25 penalty units, imprisonment for up to 30 days, or both.

CUTS argues that the distinction is important because the law provides for enforcement and prosecution where an offence is committed, rather than automatically treating every expired licence as evidence of unlawful driving.

It is therefore asking the DVLA to clarify whether the escalating amounts are approved renewal fees, administrative penalties or another form of charge.

“If the amounts are penalties, the DVLA must explain the legal process that permits an administrative system to impose them without proof of driving during the period of expiry, without a hearing and without a finding by a court,” the statement said.

Mr Adomako stressed that CUTS was not advocating driving with an expired licence.

“CUTS is not encouraging anyone to drive with an expired licence. Driving without a valid licence must attract lawful enforcement. Our concern is different: the DVLA should not presume that every person with an expired licence continued to drive, then impose an automatic escalating charge without first establishing the legal and factual basis,” he said.

Expiry does not prove driving

CUTS said the mere expiry of a licence should not automatically be equated with unlawful driving.

It noted that a licence holder could be living abroad, studying, ill or simply not driving for an extended period. Such a person, it argued, could return years later and seek to renew the licence without having driven on Ghanaian roads during the period of expiry.

Mr Adomako said such motorists should be encouraged to regularise their licences before returning to the road rather than being treated as though they had committed an offence.

“That citizen should be encouraged to regularise his licence before returning to the road. He should not be branded delinquent and punished as though expiry itself proves unlawful driving. The system must distinguish an expired document from the separate act of driving without a valid licence,” he said.

CUTS also questioned the use of the word “delinquency”, saying it could imply wrongdoing before the circumstances of an individual licence holder had been established.

It proposed the use of neutral descriptions such as “renewal after expiry”, alongside clear criteria for waivers, exemptions or proof that a vehicle was not being used.

Concern over GH¢181 data amendment fee

The think tank also raised concerns about a GH¢181 charge for amending a licence holder’s electronic records.

It argued that charging motorists to update basic information such as telephone numbers or residential addresses could discourage people from keeping their records current.

According to CUTS, accurate contact and residential information is important for road safety, identity verification, criminal investigations and emergency communication.

“The DVLA should design fees to support compliance, not discourage it. When a citizen wants to correct an address or telephone number, the Authority gains better data. Charging GH¢181 for a basic update risks leaving the database outdated and weakens the public interest the database is meant to serve,” Mr Adomako said.

CUTS has consequently called on Parliament to conduct an urgent inquiry into the legality, approval and administration of the DVLA’s escalating “delinquency” charges.

It also wants the DVLA and the Ghana Police Service to clarify their respective enforcement responsibilities so the public can clearly understand the processes for investigating, prosecuting and sanctioning drivers who operate vehicles without valid licences.

Ghana News.title: Child among three killed in Russian missile attacks near Kyiv
Ghana News.content:
At least three people, including a child, have been killed in overnight Russian attacks near the Ukrainian capital Kyiv.

In the early hours of Saturday missiles hit east of the capital and witnesses reported hearing powerful explosions just days after strikes across Ukraine killed 21 people.

Falling debris damaged apartment buildings and cars, while a fire broke out at a separate building, the head of the regional military administration Timur Tkachenko said. He added that three others had been wounded in the ballistic missile strikes.

Emergency crews were also fighting fires at a building and fuel tank in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaly Klitchko wrote on Telegram.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS shared photos showing garages, a business and a building on fire in Kyiv, adding: "The number of victims is being clarified."

President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in the Serbian capital Belgrade for his first visit after raising concerns about Ukraine's capacity to fend off Russian missile attacks due to depleting interceptor stockpiles.

Zelensky is is trying to build wider support for Ukraine, but Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has refused to apply sanctions to Russia.

Serbia is trying to join the EU and has provided aid to Ukraine and promised to help it rebuild after the war.

The two leaders were set to discuss economic ties, relations with the EU and security issues in Belgrade.

Earlier in the week, Zelensky said delays in receiving anti-ballistic systems from partners leads to "horrific casualties and destruction", saying that having a stronger interceptor capability "could have saved lives" in recent deadly assaults.

The president later said the supply of interceptors from allies had been "significantly reduced" this year.

It came after Ukraine hit two oil refineries deep inside Russia along with Moscow-linked vessels in the Black Sea, which Zelensky said was intended to limit oil revenues used by Russia to "finance" its war in Ukraine.

Recent mediation talks have faltered, leading to an escalation of attacks between both sides.

Ghana News.title: Delayed construction projects pollute air, put lives at risk
Ghana News.content:
Life for residents and workers along the Adentan–Dodowa road was upended in 2024. A routine upgrade scheduled to take three years has left the community covered in dust and harmful pollutants, putting thousands of lives at risk.

The project stalled early on, and experts say the failure to pay the contractor on time has led to delays that may mean this misery continues for the community even longer.

The project is just one of many roadworks under the government's "Big Push" infrastructure development programme across the country that are taking longer than promised. Delays, often caused by missed government payments to contractors, are leaving millions of Ghanaians exposed to increased risks of diseases linked to air pollution, such as asthma, heart disease, cancer and diabetes.

"Here in Ghana, we don't implement engineering projects well, especially government of Ghana-funded projects," said Joseph Odei, a fellow of the Ghana Institution of Engineers. He said poor oversight and corruption are among the reasons projects are delayed. "They delay paying contractors, so they face challenges and vacate the project."

The 22-kilometre Adentan–Dodowa dual carriageway stretches from the Adentan Barrier through Katamanso, Oyibi and Gbortsui to the Dodowa Hospital Junction. The project is expected to ease traffic congestion between the Greater Accra, Eastern and Volta regions while improving road safety and reducing travel time. Experts agree it would boost economic activity in the region.

The contract was awarded in March 2024 to the Ghanaian company Oswal Investments under a 36-month agreement. Inspecting the project a year later, Kwame Agbodza, Minister for Roads and Highways, conceded that the project had stalled, blaming the previous government's failure to make agreed payments. Mr Agbodza said the Mahama government had settled the outstanding payments.

Gabriel Foli, project manager for Oswal Investments, declined to comment for this story, but in July he told Channel One TV that delays were caused by property acquisition, negotiations over compensation for owners and the relocation of utility lines. He assured the public that the project was two-thirds complete and on track to be finished by March 2027.

For residents, the roadworks are taking a heavy toll. People here are well aware of the dangers.

Mary Adjiele, 50, says three of her grandchildren have developed severe coughs accompanied by high fevers since the work began. The family has been forced to spend much of its income on medical treatment at Alpha and Omega Hospital in Dodowa.

"Cough with blood," Adjiele said in Twi. "It is small streaks or drops of bright red blood that come with mucus from three of my grandchildren. The money we use for our business and family upkeep is now going into hospital bills."

Health experts warn that prolonged exposure to dust particles is dangerous. Fine particulate matter can enter the bloodstream, increasing the risk of chronic illnesses, including kidney and heart diseases, diabetes and cancer.

"Road dust often has fine particles, cement, silica and vehicle exhaust," said Dorcas Effah Agyeiwaa, a public health nurse at the community's Amamorley Clinic. "When we breathe it in, it can irritate our airways and make asthma worse. That irritation can cause the blood vessels in the airways to break and lead to blood in the cough."

Health authorities say infrastructure development in Ghana is necessary to boost economic activity, but the health impacts cannot be ignored. They say communities across the country should not be left to deal with the health consequences of delays caused by government failures.

The Ghana Health Service reports increasing cases of respiratory illnesses across the Greater Accra Region. According to Dr Robert Amesiya, Greater Accra Regional Director of Health Services, in the two years to 2023, hypertension – a disease closely linked to air pollution – was the fifth-highest cause of death in Accra, claiming 200 lives, while nearly 40,000 cases were reported. Asthma and cardiac cases also increased.

"We thank the government for building the roads for our safety," said Dr Amesiya in Twi. "But the dust on the construction roads is too much."

A spare-parts dealer operating along the road says the thick dust has made every working day a health challenge. Concerned about his wife's worsening asthma and persistent coughing, he has asked her to stop assisting him at the shop.

"We sell car parts, but the dust has filled my wife's and my nose," the dealer said in Twi. "I clean my shop every 20 minutes, but the dust keeps coming back. My wife has been coughing continuously. We have nowhere else to go because this business is our livelihood. We humbly appeal to the government to asphalt the road to reduce the dust. Our health matters too."

Provision shop owner Serwaa Ansah Opoku says the dust has left her battling constant illness.

"Because of the dust on the road, when we wear our clothes, it turns brown," she said in Twi. "We keep getting headaches. We take local herbal medicine and the drugs our doctors prescribed for us to take care of the headaches and blood pressure."

While waakye vendor Hamdia Ishmahill, a student, reports frequent coughs that have affected her business.

"It worries me. The dust has reduced our customers who buy waakye from us," the student said in Twi. "My mum is not able to come to the wayside to sell. I'm a student, so I normally come to support her. I always get coughs. But because people complain there is no food around, I'm forced to sell in the dust."

Traditional leaders are equally worried. Chief Adjie Kwashie, Linguist of Adenta Frafraha, said asthma cases within the community are increasing, with many residents complaining of worsening respiratory conditions. The traditional palace has been suspended because of the unhealthy environment.

"We have elderly people who come to our palace reporting cases of asthma," said Chief Kwashie in Twi. "We've asked them to tell the contractor to continue watering the road to reduce the dust. We've also reached out to the workers constructing the road. Once in a while, they come to sprinkle water on the road. We need asphalt on our road."

During his April 2026 visit, the Minister directed the contractor to regularly sprinkle water on the road to minimise dust and reduce its impact on surrounding communities, stressing that protecting residents' health remains the responsibility of the contractor.

"We expect a lot more speed," Minister Agbodza said in Twi, speaking with engineers and the contractor. "This is another very important corridor which, when completed, will help significantly. So pay attention to it. While you are doing it, the dust will be to the minimum. We know it is difficult. We know it's not easy to water continuously, but that is your responsibility, so don't run away from it."

Ella Christine Esinam Nongo, Municipal Chief Executive for Adentan, has assured residents that the Assembly and the contractor are working together to reduce dust pollution.

"Residents, please be a little patient with us," an Assembly official said in Twi. "If the contractors come to fix it and there are still potholes, the same people will not be happy with us. We beg you. Since we have endured bad roads for a long time, give us a little time to fix it. Anytime the contractor is not around, the Assembly sprinkles water on the road."

Dr Amesiya urged residents to wear nose masks to minimise exposure to dust while efforts continue to control pollution along the construction corridor.

This story is a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Clean Air Reporting project. Funding was provided by the Clean Air Fund, which had no say in the story's content.

Ghana News.title: Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Ghana News.content:
Gianni Infantino's alleged lover was given a severance payment over the affair by Uefa while he was its general secretary, according to a Daily Telegraph investigation, external.

A spokesman for the now Fifa president was reported to have told the paper Infantino "strongly denies these categorically untrue allegations".

Uefa, for whom Infantino was general secretary from 2009 to 2016, issued a statement confirming "a departure payment was made to the individual in question".

The allegations come as Infantino fights for his future as Fifa president following his aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

BBC Sport has contacted Fifa and Infantino for comment.

The Telegraph reported that Uefa paid a six-figure sum to the woman, who had an alleged relationship with Infantino, who is married, during his time at European football's governing body.

"Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory," a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph.

"No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino's behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved."

Uefa confirmed a payment was made to the woman in question and that it covered the fees for her to complete an MBA course at a local business school.

It said all payments were in line with regulations at the time, but those regulations have since been tightened and "reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation".

The claims put further pressure on Infantino, who is facing calls to resign as Fifa president over the World Cup private investment plan.

The 56-year-old has apologised for "errors" he made in those controversial proposals, but did not step down after receiving the backing of senior executives in a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday.

Infantino joined Uefa in 2000 and became secretary general in 2009, before being appointed Fifa president in 2016.

European teams have threatened to boycott Fifa events despite the plans being aborted, saying certain conditions have not been met.

But Conmebol - the South American confederation - and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) have backed Infantino, as have the football associations of World Cup co-hosts Mexico and tournament runners-up Argentina.

Ghana News.title: Vice President urges universities to embrace Artificial Intelligence
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has urged universities across the country to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) by integrating digital literacy and emerging technologies into their academic programmes where necessary.

Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang also called on universities to promote interdisciplinary research, support technology-based entrepreneurship and equip graduates to use Artificial Intelligence responsibly.

The Vice President made the call at the 15th Graduation Ceremony of KAAF University, where 2,053 students graduated under the theme, “Transforming Lives, Transforming Ghana.”

She encouraged the management of KAAF University to take advantage of Ghana’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to equip graduates with the knowledge and skills required to navigate an increasingly technology-driven environment.

Professor Opoku-Agyemang said KAAF University had demonstrated its commitment to producing graduates equipped with the knowledge, values and practical skills needed to succeed in a rapidly changing world.

The Vice President also highlighted the “Teacher Dabre” initiative, which seeks to provide decent accommodation for teachers and address housing challenges, particularly for educators posted to rural communities.

She said providing decent accommodation for teachers would help ensure that postings to rural communities did not become an additional hardship for educators.

Meanwhile, Chancellor of KAAF University, Michael Aidoo, has appealed to the government to extend the 'No Fees Stress' initiative to students in private tertiary institutions.

According to him, extending the initiative to students in private institutions would help reduce the financial burden on parents.

He stressed that students attending private institutions are also Ghanaians and deserve government support.

Ghana News.title: STU Lecture Equips Researchers with Strategies for Stronger Academic Papers
Ghana News.content:
The Directorate of Grants, Research and Development (DGRD) of the Sunyani Technical University (STU) has organised a public lecture to equip researchers and students with practical strategies for producing quality academic papers.

The lecture, on the theme “The Anatomy of a Strong Academic Paper in Management Studies", was delivered by Professor Samuel Adomako, Professor of Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom.

Prof. Adomako stressed the importance of precision, relevance and originality in academic writing, urging researchers to ensure their work makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge.

He advised researchers to write abstracts after completing their studies, saying an abstract should concisely capture the research gap, objectives, methodology, findings and theoretical contribution.

On writing introductions, Prof. Adomako said the opening paragraph should immediately engage readers and establish the significance of the study. He urged researchers to identify clear research gaps and frame their studies around compelling research puzzles.

He also cautioned against vague problem statements and encouraged researchers to engage with recent literature to ensure their studies address contemporary academic issues.

On theory and hypotheses, he stressed the need to select appropriate theories to guide research, describing a hypothesis as “a bridge between theory and research".

Prof. Adomako further advised researchers to clearly explain their data, samples, variables and measurement techniques in the methodology section while identifying and addressing potential biases.

For the results section, he urged researchers to present their findings clearly without unnecessarily linking them to existing literature. He also cautioned against copying raw statistical outputs directly into academic papers.

In discussing the final section, he recommended that researchers restate the purpose of their study, interpret the findings and clearly articulate their theoretical contribution.

He also encouraged researchers to examine the limitations and suggested future research directions of previous studies as a way of identifying opportunities for further research.

The Acting Pro-Vice Chancellor of STU, Prof. Evans Zoya Kpamma, supported the call for impactful research, stressing that academics should focus on contributing to knowledge rather than publishing solely for career advancement.

“We should not just be publishing for promotion’s sake, but by contributing to knowledge,” he said.

Earlier, the Director of Grants, Research and Development, Prof. Edward Owusu, said the lecture formed part of the university’s efforts to strengthen research capacity, promote intellectual discourse and advance academic excellence.

Ghana News.title: University administrators declare strike effective August 10 over market premium disparities
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has reactivated its nationwide strike effective Monday, August 10, 2026, over what it describes as persistent disparities in market premium and related allowances between teaching and non-teaching senior members in public universities.

The decision was announced in a communiqué presented by the association's newly sworn-in National President, Rev. Kwaku Karikari Amoah of the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR), at the close of GAUA's 2026 National Congress in Sunyani on Friday, August 7, 2026.

The congress, held on the theme "Building agile universities: the role of administrative and professional staff," brought together members from public universities across the country to deliberate on issues affecting their welfare and to swear in new national executives.

Delegates wore red armbands throughout the congress to protest the unfairness, while various speakers highlighted the critical role of university administrators, arguing that their contributions are often undervalued in decisions on remuneration.

In the communiqué, Congress expressed concern over what it called widening disparities in market premium.

"Congress noted with grave concern that the recent adjustments to market premium have created significant inequities between teaching and non-teaching senior members, despite both categories operating within the same analogous senior member structure," the communiqué stated.

While reaffirming its support for improved conditions of service for teaching staff, GAUA insisted that "such improvements must not result in unfair and discriminatory treatment of non-teaching senior members".

The statement recalled that following the implementation of the Single Spine Salary Structure (SSSS) in 2012, the market premium for all senior members was harmonised to ensure equity across the various categories of senior members, adding that "no upwards adjustments have been made since then until the recent review in 2026".

According to the Association, although an agreement signed with the government on April 22, 2026, secured a 40 per cent increase in the consolidated market premium and non-basic allowance for non-teaching senior members, the disparity remains substantial between the benefits received by teaching and non-teaching senior members.

It said the average teaching senior member now receives about GH¢10,000 in market premium, compared with approximately GH¢4,718 for a non-teaching senior member, "within what remains an analogous paid structure".

"It is particularly troubling that the lowest-ranked teaching senior member now receives a higher market premium than the highest-ranked non-teaching member, a registrar or a finance officer, even though both categories were placed at the same market premium level when the SSSS was introduced in 2012."

The communiqué described the situation as "inconsistent with the principles of fairness, internal equity, and the objectives of the Single Spine Pay Policy", warning that "the growing inequity threatens staff morale, industrial harmony, and effective administration of Ghana's public universities."

GAUA also disclosed that it petitioned the National Labour Commission and other relevant state institutions on July 16, 2026, seeking intervention but had yet to receive a response.

The Association maintained that its campaign is "not directed against teaching senior members" but rather seeks "equitable treatment for all senior members based on transparent, objective and consistent principles".

The communique called on the government and all relevant stakeholders to uphold the principles of fairness, equity, and equal recognition of the invaluable contribution of all senior members to the development of Ghana's public universities.

Consequently, Congress resolved that "effective Monday, 10 August 2026, the strike action previously suspended by the Association is hereby reactivated with immediate effect", adding that the industrial action will continue pending "the satisfactory resolution of the issues in dispute".

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
